The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{f({x}_{n})}{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=({e}^{-x}+{x}^{3}-2x)^{′}=-{e}^{-x}+3{x}^{2}-2.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{e}^{-{x}_{n}}+{x}_{n}^{3}-2{x}_{n}}{-{e}^{-{x}_{n}}+3{x}_{n}^{2}-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=0.5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-\frac{{e}^{-{x}_{0}}+{x}_{0}^{3}-2{x}_{0}}{-{e}^{-{x}_{0}}+3{x}_{0}^{2}-2} \\  & =0.5-\frac{{e}^{-0.5}+{0.5}^{3}-2\cdot 0.5}{-{e}^{-0.5}+3\cdot {0.5}^{2}-2} \\  & ≈0.355,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
